u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows You World Map\\n\\tLets You Move Units and Resources\\n\\tAllows You to See Enemy Settlements\"

u\"\\tThis is the main view of your interface - it fills the upper two-thirds of the screen. This view toggles between displaying the entire world or showing a specific settlement. Military units are shown in stacks of unit types. The types are infantry, armor, air, sea, transports, missiles, and special units. Each stack has several units in it that move as a group. Right click the stack to move or view individual units.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface Toolbar\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tChanges Screen Between the Planet and Territory Views.\"
u\"\\tThis button switches the screen between the Planet and Territory Views.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tAlways\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Move Around Planet and Territory Views\\n\\tLets You Quickly Move Units Between Territories\"

u\"\\tThe map in the lower right is the Satellite View. By clicking one of its territories, you change what you see in your Territory and Planet View. Use this to see other territories or other parts of the planet. Units may also be dragged and dropped onto the Satellite View. This lets you move these units quickly.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows How Much Money You Have\\n\\tLets You Change Your Tax Rate\"

u\"\\tThis button shows you how much money you have. Click it to see how much money you will get from taxes next turn. You can either set an overall tax rate for your colony or adjust a specific territory's tax rate. Increasing taxes raises money but makes colonists unhappy. Certain buildings, like shipyards and airports, give you additional trade income. Selling resources to another colony also may add to your funds.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDisplays Current Turn Number\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tBrings Up The File Menu\"

u\"\\tClicking here gives you access to all your file functions: save, load, quit, new game, and so on. It also lets you get to your Play Options screen, where you can manipulate a variety of settings.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Choose Your Technology Research Strategy \"

u\"\\tPress this button to bring up the Technology Tree. From here you see what technologies have been completed, which one is in progress, and which technologies are ready for you to study. Multiple technologies may be queued up in a research order, letting you create long range strategies. You may also change what you are researching from here.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\tTechnology Tree\\n\\tColony Assistant\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows Research Progress\"

u\"\\tWatch your research progress with this bar graph. The green area is research you have finished, while the yellow area shows how far your research advances next turn. Building more Universities, Tech Labs, and Collective Tech Labs increases your research rate.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tReviews Your Events\"

u\"\\tThis button lets you look at all the events that happened this turn. It shows you a menu of tabs. Events you haven't looked at yet are lit, while events you've seen are not. If a category did not have an event this turn, it is grayed out. You watch all your battles from the Event Log.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tSends Messages to Other Colonies\"

u\"\\tGo ahead, talk to another colony! Do this by selecting an insult, praise, threat, brag, or complaint. You can also type a custom message in the message box. Then choose the race or races you wish to send the message to and press the Send button.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Make, Observe, and Break Pacts With Other Players \"

u\"\\tMake pacts with other players using this button. Propose a specific pact with a given player or break an existing one. Computer colonies only accept a pact with you if they have good feelings towards you. Pacts can either be broken by a diplomatic announcement or by a devious hidden action. Existing pacts between all the colonies are also displayed here.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tContacts the Skirineen\"

u\"\\tPress this button to speak with the outlaw Skirineen. Be prepared to wait; they'll respond to you when they feel like it. Buy resources, information, technologies, and military units from them at slightly inflated prices. You can also sell resources to them. If your colonists catch you dealing with the Skirineen, you will have a scandal - severely reducing your morale.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows You a Territory's Morale\\n\\tDetails Why a Territory's Morale Is Changing\"

u\"\\tThis button displays morale changes in the selected territory. If green is highlighted, morale is improving. However, if red is highlighted, morale is dropping. Many things hurt your colony's spirit. High taxes make colonists angry. Starving and overpopulated colonists eventually rebel or die off. Even units patrolling a territory can lower morale.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Change Between Seeing\\n\\tResources or Military Units\"

u\"\\tThis button toggles the Planet View between showing either your military units or you resources. Both military units and resources can be moved by clicking and dragging them. You can move them to another territory using either the Planet View or the Satellite View. When resources are moved, you get a box asking how many resources you are transporting. When moving military unit stacks, you move all of a given type - air, armor, sea, missiles, transports, infantry, or special units. Right click these stacks to give units specific orders and missions.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Change Tasks Without\\n\\tMicromanaging Buildings\"

u\"\\tThe Colony Assistant lets you move colonists between tasks in a territory without dealing with separate buildings. Each task this settlement can do has a task button. This button is labeled by its name and a two numbers. The first number shows you how many colonists currently work on that task. The second shows you how many total colonists can be assigned to that task. A button displays the territory's maximum production for the specific task - totaling together all that territory's buildings. Drag colonists from one task to another to change what they are working on. You can also control military unit production from here. Use the Satellite View to switch between different territories.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tTerritory View Only\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Choose a Building\"
u\"\\tClick this button to construct a building. Choose the building you need and press Done. Your mouse arrow now has this building attached to it. Place it in the square or squares you want.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tTerritory View Only\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDestroys a Selected Building or Settlement\"

u\"\\tWhen you press this button, the mouse arrow changes to a demolish icon. Choose the unwanted building in the Territory View or settlement in the Planet View. The building or settlement is immediately demolished, returning half of its construction resources to your stockpile. When demolishing a settlement in the Planet View, you will not destroy a shrine.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDisplays Your Score and Scenario Objectives\"

u\"\\tUse this button to check on your current score and review a scenario's victory objectives. Any objectives you have already completed will have a check next to them. Also all the players and their handicaps are listed here.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tAllows You To See Resources so You Can Better Place Buildings\"

u\"\\tUsing this feature transforms your Territory View into a flattened version, showing the foundations of your buildings and the resource values of the territory's squares. Each time the button is pressed, it toggles to display a new resource critical to building placement. Eventually it will cycle back to normal view. Pressing the <INSERT> key is a useful shortcut to using this feature.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\tColony Assistant\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tChanges The Resource Bar Between Territory and Planet Views\"

u\"\\tBy clicking this toggle, you change the Toolbar's readouts between the Planet and Territory Views. This does not change the map view, but it does change what your Toolbar displays. When the world is highlighted, you are looking at your entire colony's statistics. When the area inside the toggle is lit, your Toolbar shows you the statistics of the selected territory.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\tColony Assistant\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows Your Total Resources\"

u\"\\tYour colony's resource stockpile is shown along the bottom of your screen. Under each resource are two numbers. The first number is how much of that resource you have. The second number shows how much of that resource is being produced this turn. These resource icons can be dragged to a territory in the either Planet or Satellite Views.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows How Many Colonists You Have\"

u\"\\tThese two icons display your colony's population. This shows you either your colony's or a selected territory's total population. The top icon tells you how many happy colonists are in the territory or colony. The bottom icon displays your unhappy colonists.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\tColony Assistant\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tGives You Information\"
u\"\\tThis button lets you contact me, Oolan. I offer my help to all colony leaders. If you click the Help button, it brings up all my information, letting you to search for a desired topic.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tEnds Your Turn and Starts A New One\\n\\tDisplays How Much Time You Have Left\"
u\"\\tPress this button and your turn ends. After a short time a new turn will start. If you are playing a timed game, a readout inside the button displays how many seconds you have left in a turn.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tArmy Window\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\tCombat Window\\n\\nWhat They Are\\n\\tEach Colony's Flag Color\"

u\"\\tEach race has a separate map color. All units, flags, and other icons have this same color. The colony colors are:\\n\\n\\tCHCH-T: Orange\\n\\tCYTH: Black\\n\\tHUMAN: Gray\\n\\tMAUG: Blue\\n\\tRE'LU: Aqua\\n\\tTARTH: Red\\n\\tUVA MOSK: Grass Green\"
u\"Purpose\\n\\tUse the Colony Assistant to\\n\\tChange the Labor Priorities in a Territory\"

u\"\\tThe Colony Assistant has different task buttons. Each task button displays the task name, the number or colonists who are working it, and the maximum number of colonists that can be on that task. Clicking a task button moves its colonists to the Labor Pool window below. From here colonists can be dropped onto another task button. Clicking and dragging from any task button moves one colonist at a time. Colonists can also be dragged to the Satellite View and dropped onto other territories.\"
u\"Purpose\\n\\tUse the Colony Assistant to\\n\\tManufacture Military Units\"

u\"\\tThe Colony Assistant has a queue that shows what military units are in production. This queue changes its display when different task buttons are selected. The add (+) and delete (-) buttons let you change the queue. Units at the top of the queue are completed first.\"
u\"Purpose\\n\\tUse the Colony Assistant to\\n\\tCreate Needed Resources\"

u\"\\tResource production can be increased and decreased by moving colonists on and off the different resource tasks. The Resource Bar below shows you how your resource production is changing. The Resource Bar can show resource changes in either your entire colony or a specific settlement.\"
u\"\\tSee any battles you fought this turn. If you do not want to watch the battle, you can jump right to the results.\"
u\"What It Shows\\n\\tYour New Technologies, Buildings, or Units\"
u\"\\tThis displays all the new technologies, units, and buildings you gained this turn.\"
u\"\\tThis lists any special events which occurred - such as earthquakes, ion storms, or population explosions.\"
u\"\\tThis screen calls attention to any energy shortages, morale problems, empty building queues, and other problems which threaten your colony.\"
u\"What It Shows\\n\\tThe Success or Failure of\\n\\tMilitary Unit Missions\"
u\"\\tThis window lets you know when military units gain experience, repair themselves, spy successfully, are transferred, and so on. New settlements are also listed here.\"
u\"\\tResources are moved automatically every turn. All these transportation costs are listed here in detail.\"
u\"Can Be Done In\\n\\tPlanet View\\n\\tTerritory View\\n\\tArmy Window\\n\\nWhat They Do\\n\\tDefend and Expand Your Colony\"

u\"\\tUnits are grouped together in stacks. Move these stacks by clicking and dragging them. There are seven different stack types – armor, infantry, sea, air, tranports, missiles, or special units. When a stack is moved all the units of that type in the territory move together. Left-clicking a stack opens the Army Window, displaying the individual units of the stack. Right-clicking a stack is a shortcut, opening both the Army Window and the Unit Orders Box. In the Territory View, the Army Box is opened by clicking the main interface's View Army button. Once the  Army Window is open, left-clicking on a unit selects it, while right-clicking a unit lets you to issue orders. These units are individually moved by dragging them to other territories in either the Planet or Satellite Views. You can move units as  a group by selecting more than one and then dragging any member of that group to another territory.\"
u\"Can Be Done In\\n\\tPlanet View\\n\\tTerritory View\\n\\tArmy Window\\n\\nWhat They Do\\n\\tAttack Other Colonies at Range\"

u\"\\tYou launch a missile by clicking and dragging it into another territory. When a missile stack is launched, it moves all the missiles in that territory. Bringing up the Army Window displays all the individual missiles in a given territory. These single units can then be clicked and dragged to the Satellite View to launch them separately at a territory. Right-clicking any missile in the Army Window brings up the Unit Properties Box, letting you assign it a target.\"
u\"Can Be Done In\\n\\tPlanet View\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tLets You Manipulate Military Unit Stacks\"

u\"\\tThe Planet View's unit stacks represent a cluster of similarly classed units. These unit classes are armor, infantry, sea, tranports, air, missiles, and special. A number on each stack icon shows how many units it contains. Moving that icon moves all the units in the stack. Left-clicking it opens the Army Window, displaying all the individual units in the stack. As a shortcut for assigning group orders, right-clicking a stack opens both the Army Window and the Unit Orders Box. Once the Army Window is open, left-clicking on a unit selects it, while right-clicking on the unit lets you issue it orders. These units are individually moved by dragging them to other territories in either the Planet or Satellite Views.\"
u\"Can Be Done In\\n\\tTerritory View\\n\\tPlanet View\\n\\tColony Assistant\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tMoves Colonists to Different Buildings or Settlements\"

u\"\\tYou can move colonists either between buildings or between settlements. In the Territory View, drag and drop colonists between buildings to change where they work within that settlement. They can also be placed on the Satellite View to move them between territories you own. In the Planet View, you can also drag colonists between territories. Use the Colony Assistant to drag colonists between task buttons or even move them to new territories by dragging and dropping them in the Satellite View.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tTerritory View\\n\\tColony Assistant\\n\\tBuilding Properties Box\\n\\nWhat They Do\\n\\tChange Production Priorities\"

u\"\\tColonists work in the buildings you place them on, so you can click and drag colonists to buildings where you wish them to work. However, you can also drag them between tasks in either the Colony Assistant or the Building Properties Box. Right click any building to bring up this box. Note that each building has a colonist limit. For instance, a City Center can only have 800 colonists (8 icons) in it.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tFood\\n\\tTaxes\\n\\tMilitary Units\\n\\tOverpopulation\\n\\tBlack Market\\n\\tCloning\\n\\tHospitals\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tChanges Colonist Productivity\"

u\"\\tPlentiful food, low taxes, culture, and art objects keep colonists happy and productive. Starvation, high taxes, overpopulation, cloning, black market deals, destroyed shrines, and patrolling units drop morale. Once morale drops below 90%, some colonists stop working.\"
u\"Affected by\\n\\tNumber of Colonists\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tChanges Resource and Unit Production\"

u\"\\tYou assign colonists to work in different buildings. Do this by either clicking and dragging colonists between buildings or by moving them between task buttons inside the Colony Assistant. Each building has a colonist limit. For instance, a City Center can only have 800 colonists (8 icons) in it. In the Colony Assistant, buildings that share a task are grouped together to create that task button's colonist limit. Since City Centers, Shipyards, and Airports all produce trade income, their colonist limits are added together on the Trade task button.\"

u\"Affected By\\n\\tFarm Production\\n\\tCrop Plagues\\n\\tCyth Poison Land Mission\\n\\tWeather Control Station\\n\\tTidal Vortex Generator\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tHelps Morale, Population Growth, and Sustains Military Forces\"

u\"\\tA food surplus keeps your colonists happy. If colonists starve morale drops quickly and colonists start to die off. Food is also important for maintaining your military forces. Farms, Hydroponic Farms, Kelp Farms, and Food Replicators all produce this important resource. Weather Control Stations and Tidal Vortex Generators can be used to increase your food production.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tTax Rate\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tIncreases or Decreases Your Income Per Turn\"

u\"\\tYou collect taxes every turn. Each tax level has a positive or negative impact on morale. You can also tax some territories more than others. This lets you fleece populated areas for more money and give tax breaks to territories with a smaller population.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tRoad Type\\n\\tOceans\\n\\tTerritory Ownership\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tAssigns Transportation Costs\"

u\"\\tTransportation through friendly territories costs 0-2 credits. Resources moved over neutral territories and oceans cost 3-4 credits. Resources can not be moved across enemy territories. Players can thus create blockades which cut off enemy troops and settlements from the main colony. Researching Hoverway and Transporters reduces transportation costs.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tShipyards\\n\\tAirports\\n\\tFactories\\n\\tCity Centers\\n\\tSea Housing\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tIncreases Your Money\"
u\"\\tSome buildings give you extra income through trade. Shipyards and Airports generate the most income. Factories and City Centers also make you some money.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tCity Centers\\n\\tCulture Centers\\n\\tMuseums\\n\\tSea Housing\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tIncreases Your Colonists' Morale\"

u\"\\tCulture offsets bad morale. For example, heavy taxes costs you five morale points. Creating five culture points counters all of this bad morale. Only City Centers, Culture Centers, Sea Housing, Museums, and certain Shrines make culture.\"

u\"\\tA planet will be one of seven environments - and each environment changes the resource amounts found on them. These environment changes can be shut off in the Scenario Setup screen.\\n\\n\\tAlien - High Endurium (a metal), Low Iron\\n\\tVolcanic - High Metals/ High Energy\\n\\tEarth-like - Balanced Resources\\n\\tTropical - High Food/ Low Metals\\n\\tMartian - Low Energy\\n\\tIcy - Low Wood\\n\\tDry - Low Food\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tAffects Resource Production\\n\\tAids Population Growth\"
u\"\\tPlains are an ideal for starting a colony. Food usually grows best on plains. Your population also grows the fastest on plains.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tAffects Resource Production\\n\\tAids Population Growth\"
u\"\\tForests are good places to begin your colony, as they produce every natural resource in modest amounts. They never produce large amounts of anything but wood.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tAffects Resource Production\\n\\tSlow Population Growth\"

u\"\\tMountain territories have large amounts of iron. However, your population grows very slowly on this terrain. Ground units must go around the mountains on these territories' back edges before they can start fighting in these areas.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tAffects Resource Production\\n\\tSlow Population Growth\"
u\"\\tEnergy is easily produced in swamps, however the damp conditions severely limit your population's growth.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tRequires Ships for Transportation\"

u\"\\tUntil you build ships, AAVs, or airplanes, you cannot move across ocean territories. A shipyard lets you construct ships. Some ships can transport military units over ocean territories. You can also build Sea Platforms which allow you to settle ocean territories.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tPoor Resource Production\\n\\tPoor Population Growth\"

u\"\\tVery little can be produced in wastelands, so wastelands are not a good place to build a settlement. They are useful in a military strategy. You could build a fuel depot in a wasteland to increase your military's range.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tSettlement Map\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tChanges Resource Production\\n\\tChanges Population Growth\"

u\"\\tEach square's terrain changes a resource's production. Flat ground and squares next to water are great for raising food. Cracked earth gives you energy bonuses. Rocky soil is best for mining metals, and wooded areas are ideal for harvesting lumber. Press the <Insert> key to view a settlement's resource potential in all the available squares, or simply double click or right click the square in question in order to see all of that square's resource potential.\"
u\"Affected By\\n\\tSettlement Map\\n\\tUva Mosk Shaman Mission\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tGives You a Resource Production Bonus\"

u\"\\tSome squares have a resource icon on them. These are special resource bonuses. Production of this resource is nearly doubled on that square! An Uva Mosk Command Corps unit set to the Shaman mission has a chance of creating these bonuses on its own\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tTaxes\\n\\tTrade\\n\\tBlack Market\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tMaking Buildings and Military Units\"

u\"\\tThere are several ways to make money. Taxes give you credits each turn. City Centers, Factories, Airports, and Shipyards can all raise money through trade. You can sell resources to another colony. You may even sell resources to the Skirineen Black Market.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tColonists\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tResource and Unit Production\"

u\"\\tEach building has a colonist limit. For instance, a Culture Center may only have 400 colonists (4 icons) making culture. Click and drag your colonists on the buildings where you want them to work or move them from task to task in the Colony Assistant. Each task button in the Colony Assistant represents the total labor force that can work on that task. A task button's total labor is added together from all the buildings that share that task. For instance, City Centers, Shipyards, Airports, Shrines, and Factories all make trade. Their colonist limits are added together; this creates the total number of colonists that can work on the Trade task button in that settlement.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tFarms\\n\\tKelp Farms\\n\\tHydroponic Farms\\n\\tFood Replicators\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tFeeding Colonists and Military Units\"

u\"\\tFood grows on Farms, Hydroponic Farms, Kelp Farms, Shrines and Food Replicators. Placing farms in flat areas produce the most food while farms in rocky areas raise the least. Also placing a farm over a food bonus icon boosts production. It is critical to maintain your food supplies. If they drop below your needs, your colonists start to die and your military units begin to disband.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tFarms\\n\\tHydroponic Farms\\n\\tFood Replicators\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tConstructing Buildings\"

u\"\\tWood is cut by farms. Farms placed over lightly and heavily forested areas produce the most wood. Also areas with a wood bonus icon increase the amount of wood cut. Note that Kelp Farms only produce food.\"

u\"\\tEnergy is generated by Nuclear Plants, Fusion Plants, Tidal Energy Plants, Shrines, and Anti-Matter Plants. The best territory to generate power in is a swamp territory. Also power plants built on bonus energy squares make extra energy.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tSurface Mines\\n\\tMantle Drills\\n\\tSub-Space Magnet\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tMaking Buildings\\n\\tConstructing Military Units\"

u\"\\tSurface Mines, Mantle Drills, Shrines, and Sub-Space Magnets all produce iron. Mountain regions are the best places to build a mine. Also rocky ground and iron bonus squares give you high ore production.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tSurface Mines\\n\\tMantle Drills\\n\\tSub-Space Magnet\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tMore Efficient Construction of Buildings and Units \"
u\"\\tThis metal cannot be mined until your colony has researched the technology Endurium Mining. A rare ore, endurium has five times the metal value of iron.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tPower Plants\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tHigh Level Military Units and Buildings\"

u\"\\tResearch Anti-Matter Containment and you can generate this powerful resource. Anti-matter pods are massive power cells needed for high level weapons. All power plants produce anti-matter pods. Some Shrines may also produce anti-matter pods as well.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tFactories\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tBuildings and Military Units\"

u\"\\tSteel cannot be refined until Metallurgy is researched. Once this technology is finished all Factories, Automated Factories, and Metal Replication Stations get the Iron into Steel task. Steel has five times the metal value of iron.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tFactories\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tHigh Level Buildings and Units\"

u\"\\tTriidium Processing must be researched before this super-hard alloy can be refined. Once Triidium Processing is achieved, all Factories, Automated Factories, and Metal Replication Stations get the Endurium to Triidium task. Triidium has ten times the metal value of iron.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tUniversities\\n\\tTech Labs\\n\\tCollective Tech Labs\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tMaking Buildings and Military Units\"
u\"\\tResearching Electronics lets you manufacture this resource. Universities, Tech Labs, and Collective Tech Labs all manufacture electronic parts.\"
u\"Made By\\n\\tArt Complexes\\n\\tShrines\\n\\nUsed For\\n\\tRaising Morale\\n\\tIncreasing Money\"

u\"\\tArt objects are created only by Art Complexes. Each art object permanently raises morale by two points in that territory, as colonists feel that the object reflects their struggles. Art can also be sold to other colonies or on the Black Market.\"
u\"Happens In\\n\\tAll Buildings\\n\\nWhat This Does\\n\\tChanges Resource Stockpile\"

u\"\\tAs your colony grows, it needs more resources. This causes you to use up more resources than you make. To increase your colony's production, research improved technologies, construct more buildings, and expand your territories.\"
u\"Happens In\\n\\tAll Territories\\n\\nWhat This Does\\n\\tLets You Transport Resources Between Territories\"

u\"\\tResources are automatically moved to territories that need them. You may also move resources manually at a higher cost. While in the Planet View, press the Resources/Military Units toggle. This shows the resource icons in each territory. You may also change the Resource Bar so that it only displays one settlement's stockpile. You can then drag icons from there to territories in the Planet or Satellite View. Either way a box appears, asking you how much of this resource you wish to transport.\"
u\"Happens In\\n\\tPlanet View or Resource Bar\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tAllows You to Trade Resources to Other Territories\"

u\"\\tBy dragging a resource icon to the Trade button or to a rival colony, you activate the Trade Offer box. This lets you set a price and then send this bid to a race of your choosing. The prospective buyer gets a Trade Receipt box displaying your offer; they can either accept or reject it.\"
u\"All Metal Resources Have a Value Amount\\n\\nWhat This Does\\n\\tGives Metal Resources a Construction Rating\"

u\"\\tIron, endurium, steel, and triidium are all metals. Iron is the least valuable while triidium is the most valuable. The more valuable the metal the faster buildings and units are made, as less metal is needed to build them. Steel and endurium are five times as valuable as iron, while triidium is ten times as valuable.\"

u\"\\tAdvanced Medicine allows you to build Hospitals which heal Militia units. They also prevent plagues from occurring in their home territories. This technology also lets you create Medics in your City Centers. Medics rapidly heal infantry units that suffer damage in a battle.\"
u\"\\tMuch energy is released from the fusion atomic reaction. Gaining Nuclear Fusion allows you to build the Fusion Plant.\"
u\"Level One\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tNo Technology\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tElectronic Parts\\n\\tLets you build Scout and Command Corps in a City Center.\"

u\"\\tOnce you have achieved Electronics, your Universities, Tech Labs, and Collective Tech Labs are able to manufacture electronic parts. Also both Command Corps and Scouts cannot be made without this resource.\"
u\"\\tOnce you have researched Metallurgy, all your factories can convert iron ore into steel.\"
u\"Level Two\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tAdvanced Medicine and Metallurgy\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tHydroponic Farm\"

u\"\\tDeveloping Synthetic Fertilizer eliminates a farm's dependence on soil for nutrients. Synthetic Fertilizer has all the nutrients needed for healthy plant growth and increases food production. This technology lets you build the Hydroponic Farm\"
u\" Level Two\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tNuclear Fusion and Metallurgy\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tFusion Cannon\\n\\tAAV\"
u\"\\tThese mobile cannon fire a powerful fusion beam at any target. Upon impact, the beam's molecules combine, releasing much raw, destructive energy.\"

u\"\\tShockwave Projectors emit sound waves at an extremely high frequency, shaking apart both ships and airplanes. These weapons arm the highly destructive Shockwave Dreadnought. The Hydroport may also be built - an advanced ship manufacturing complex.\"

u\"\\tMolecular Bonding is a process necessary for building the Mantle Drill. This technique makes molecules cling, or bond, to a treated surface. The Mantle Drill then attracts molten iron and endurium particles inside the drill.\"

u\"\\tCloning technology allows your genetic engineers to create duplicate colonists at high speed. This is done at a Cloning Center. However, this unpopular process makes your population uneasy - lowering morale.\"
u\"\\tArm your infantry with Surface-Air Missiles to take out enemy aircraft and missiles. SAM Troopers can attack both ground and air targets quite effectively.\"
u\"\\tDeveloping Rocketry allows you to construct a Missile Base. Once the Missile Base is finished you may start building missile units.\"
u\"Level Two\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tElectronics and Nuclear Fusion\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tTech Lab\"

u\"\\tThe Chaos Theory helps these special computers glide through many complex permutations. They speed up research tremendously and aid in making electronic parts. This technology lets you build the Tech Lab.\"
u\"\\tStreamline factory production with this computerized conveyer system.  Automation improves the processing within a factory, letting you make the much faster Automated Factory.\"
u\"\\tHoverways reduce your transportation costs. These air cushioned roads push huge air barges between your territories, saving you money. All transport costs are reduced by one third.\"
u\"Level Two\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tNuclear Fusion\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tFlak Launchers\\n\\tFlak Ships\"
u\"\\tFlak technology allows you to build Flak Launchers and Flak Ships, which provide a tough defense against air and missile attacks.\"
u\"Level Two\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tNuclear Fusion\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tMilitary Airbase\\n\\tIncreases Airplane Range\"

u\"\\tThis high octane fuel burns efficiently, allowing aircraft fly to an additional territory each turn. This fuel also powers high speed construction machinery, letting you build the Military Airbase.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tFlak and Chaos Computers\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tAnti-Matter Plant\\n\\tAnti-Matter Pod Production\"

u\"\\tThese containment fields allow you to trap anti-matter and store them in pods. This is the key resource needed in several destructive weapons. Once you have this technology you may build the Anti-Matter Power Plant.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tSAM Missile\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tEnergy Defense Forts\"

u\"\\tBy bombarding an area with beams of energy, these dishes can take out many attacking units. An Energy Defense fortification is ideal for defending a territory against a Fusion Cannon onslaught.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tFusion Cannon and Neutrionic Fuel\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tEndurium Processing \"
u\"\\tThe ultra-hard endurium ore can be mined when a special magnetic system sifts through crushed metal and rock. Endurium has five times the metal value of Iron.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tSynthetic Fertilizer and Automation\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tDestroyers\"
u\"\\tUnderwater Tracking gives a ship improved ability to detect Attack Submarines. This technology allows your Shipyards to build sub-seeking Destroyers.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tShockwave Projector and Cloning\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tAttack Submarine\"

u\"\\tZero Friction Hulls are made of a dynamic material whose controlled molecular vibrations make a hull pass through water with almost no resistance. Once you have achieved this technology, your shipyards can begin turning out Attack Submarines.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tChaos Computers and Rocketry\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tIncreased Accuracy of All Fortifications\\n\\tLets Your Missile Units Have Specific Targets\"

u\"\\tTargeting Computers coordinate a wide variety of sensor input to refine a target's location. They are installed in your defense installations to improve their accuracy. Your missile units also employ Targeting Computers to let you select specific targets for them.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tNeutrionic Fuel and Flak\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tStarflare Bomber\"

u\"\\tStarflare Bombs cause massive amounts of destruction. These huge self-propelled weapons are fired from a special ground attack aircraft - the Starflare Bomber. You build Starflare Bombers in your airports.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tHoverway and Molecular Bonding\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tStronger Buildings\\n\\tAllows Building of Sea Platforms\\n\\tCivilian Defense Bunkers\"

u\"\\tAdvanced Structures technology provides your engineers with techniques that allow them to construct tougher buildings. The technology also lets you make Sea Platform Builders in your Shipyards.\"
u\"Level Three\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tRocketry and SAM Missiles\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tMine Fields\"

u\"\\tProximity Detectors are advanced sensors that can distinguish between friendly and enemy units. This technology allows you to drop Minefields both on land and the sea territories. These defenses will not damage you or your ally's units.\"

u\"\\tArming infantry with Anti-Matter Rifles lets you outfit Battle Troopers. Anti-matter containment fields are reduced to the size of a large bullet. These small fields can then be fired from this special rifle.\"
u\"Level Four\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tZero Friction Hulls\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tShockwave Carrier\\n\\tGroundbreaker Warhead\"

u\"\\tIonic Weapons concentrate the destructive effects of an ion storm. All Shockwave Carriers are armed with small scale ion guns. Also the Groundbreaker Warhead uses ion particles to create vibrations, letting these warheads burrow into the ground before exploding.\"
u\"Level Four\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tUnderwater Tracking and Advanced Structures\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tIncreased Combat Speed\\n\\tIncreased Rate of Fire\"

u\"\\tPower Cells enable you to pack more energy into each military unit - increasing vehicle speed and firing rate. All your units receive the power cell upgrade as soon as the technology is developed.\"
u\"\\tConverting endurium ore into triidium gives you a tremendous advantage. Triidium has ten times the metal value of iron.\"
u\"Level Four\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tTargeting Computers and Proximity Detectors\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tImproved Planet View\\n\\tAnti-Colony Assault Silo\"

u\"\\tLaunching these low orbit satellites lets you see more of the planet's surface. Because of the deeper silos needed to launch surveillance satellites, the Anti-Colony Assault Silo is now possible.\"
u\"Level Four\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tTargeting Computers and Anti-Matter Containment\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tCollective Tech Lab\"
u\"\\tCortex Scanners are neural implants that directly link minds together. Your scientists are then able to rapidly research technologies. You may then build the Collective Tech Lab.\"
u\"Level Four\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tStarflare Bombs and Anti-Matter Containment\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tImproves the Mental Strength\\n\\tof Your Military Units\"

u\"\\tPsi Helmets improve the psionic prowess of your military forces. Thus Command Corps units with mind control or mind blast abilities have increased power, while units that do not have these abilities are made more resist to these mental attacks. It does not give a race new abilities - it only sharpens existing ones.\"

u\"\\tPlacing a fusion beam inside an anti-matter containment field creates the volatile Disruptor Beam. Disruptor beams need large equipment to operate, so this beam is only used as an artillery weapon. A Disruptor Cannon is a vicious armor unit.\"
u\"Level Five\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tIon Weapons\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tKnowledge of All Shrine Locations\\n\\tShrine Output Doubled\"

u\"\\tBy mastering the dialect of the indigenous natives, much more information is revealed to you. You will know all the locations of the world's shrines. Plus your understanding of the native tongue helps you improve your use of these ancient structures.\"
u\"Level Five\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tPsi Helmet and Triidium Processing\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tReplication Station\"

u\"\\tMetal Replication technology lets you build a Metal Replication Station. This advanced factory duplicates metal and produces military units at a greatly accelerated rate. Automated Factories may be upgraded to Metal Replication Stations once this technology is completed.\"
u\"Level Five\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tPower Cells and Anti-Matter Rifle\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tFood Replicators\"
u\"\\tFood Replication clones existing food supplies - really increasing food production. This technology makes it possible to build the highly productive Food Replicator.\"
u\"Level Five\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tOrbital Surveillance Systems and Cortex Scanner\\n\\nGives You \\n\\tAnti-Matter Defense Forts\"

u\"\\tThis technology lets you construct Anti-Matter Defense fortifications. They are the most powerful stationary guns you can build. These guns can completely obliterate Disruptor Cannon and Battle Troopers.\"

u\"\\tThis scanner searches sub-space for iron and endurium molecules. Once it finds these molecules it pulls them into an assembling area where the ore materializes. These Sub-Space Magnets mine large amounts of iron and endurium.\"

u\"\\tElectronically enhanced assault shields provide excellent cover from most weaponry. When soldiers are fitted with these special shields they become nearly unstoppable. Assault Troopers are the toughest infantry unit you can place on the battlefield.\"
u\"Level Five\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tIon Weapons and Power Cells\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tTidal Vortex Generators\"

u\"\\tVortex Emitters are molecular-level control fields which allow you to build Tidal Vortex Generators. These structures control the motion of water within its range, sinking all enemy ships who unknowingly cruise in these oceans. If there are any friendly sea units in the territory no ships will be sunk. Vortex Emitters give Sea Platforms an added defensive capability.\"
u\"Level Five\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tPsi Helmet and Cortex Scanner\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tSupernova Spyjet\"

u\"\\tA technology which successfully blocks most scanning devices. Cloaking lets you build the Supernova Spyjet, the epitome of military aircraft. Not only does the Spyjet have high attack strength against both air and ground targets, it also can carry out spy missions.\"
u\"Level Six\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tDisruptor Beam and Sub-space Scanner\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tHolocaust Cannon\\n\\tSupernova Warhead\"

u\"\\tUsing anti-matter as a weapon is dangerous. However redesigning and strengthening anti-matter containment fields makes it possible to create the Anti-Matter Beam. These beams can be both fired from Holocaust Cannon and housed inside Supernova Warheads.\"
u\"Level Six\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tFood Replication and Assault Armor\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tCloak Mission\"
u\"\\tCertain ground units can be effectively equipped with an improved cloaking device. Advanced Cloaking gives your infantry units, Sea Transports, and Colonizers a cloak mission.\"

u\"\\tThis technology lets your Command Corps uncloak all invisible units in a territory. The Command Corps units project a special EC band that makes these units easier to see, forcing them to fight.\"
u\"Level Six\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tNative Languages and Vortex Emitters\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tWeather Control Stations\"

u\"\\tUsing an enhanced version of Vortex Emitter technology, Mesotronic Generators allow the control of air currents. These manipulations are performed in Weather Control Stations. Weather Control Stations aid friendly territories and harm unfriendly territories and air units within its range.\"
u\"Level Seven\\n\\nRequires\\n\\tAnti-Matter Beam, Advanced Cloaking, and Uncloaking\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tIncreased Unit Movement\\n\\tRemoves Transport Costs\"

u\"\\tTransporters break non-living materials down to the molecular level and transports them across great distances. This reduces transportation costs by two-thirds and lets you penetrate blockades. Also fuel can be transported into all military units.\"
u\"Requires\\n\\nAll Other Technologies\\n\\nLeads To\\n\\tVictory!\\n\\nGives You\\n\\tResource Production Bonus\"

u\"\\tTransporter and Replication technology can be combined to create a time wave. This wave is projected over the entire colony. Time advances inside the wave so your colonists can make extra resources and credits.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tPlace New Buildings for Construction In Your Settlement\\n\\nHow To Activate It\\n\\tPress The Buildings Button on the Toolbar\"

u\"\\tWhen you are in the Territory View, you can construct new buildings. Press the Buildings button to see a window that shows you all the buildings you can construct. Click on the one you want. Your mouse arrow will now have the building attached to it. Place your building down on the territory square or squares you want it on, then drag colonists onto this site to finish its construction. To choose the best location for your building, look at each square's resource potential by pressing the <Insert> key on your keyboard.\"

u\"\\tHousing increases your population. The more empty houses you have the faster your population will grow. Colonists eventually upgrade Housing to an Apartment Complex. Housing supports up to 500 colonists (5 icons). These buildings take up one square in the Territory View.\"

u\"\\tAn Apartment Complex supports 1000 (10 icons) colonists. You cannot build an Apartment Complex directly, it can only be upgraded from basic Housing. Colonists eventually upgrade Apartment Complexes to Luxury Housing. The more empty Apartment Complexes you have the faster your population grows. These buildings take up one square in your settlement.\"

u\"\\tThe largest housing complex, Luxury Housing holds up to 1500 (15 icons) colonists. You cannot build Luxury Housing directly, this structure can only be upgraded from an Apartment Complex. You will never need more than 4 luxury housing units in any territory. These buildings take up one square in your settlement. Be aware that morale drops in overpopulated territories.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Structures\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tKeeps Colonists Safe from Combat\"

u\"\\t The Civilian Defense Bunker shelters your colonists from battle – preventing them from turning into Militia and being killed. This leaves the battle to your normal military units. They also counter the negative effect to morale caused by units on the patrol mission within your settlement. Each bunker may hold 5,000 colonists (50 icons). Note that if you lose an invasion, all your colonists in the bunker are lost. These buildings take up one square in your settlement and are not specifically targettable by other units.\"
u\"\\tCloning Centers increase population growth rates, but cause a drop in morale. These buildings take up one square on your settlement map.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tFood and Wood\"

u\"\\tFarms produce both food and wood. Usually they do best in plains or forest territories, although resource square bonuses also can help production in mountains and swamps. Farms take up four squares in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tSynthetic Fertilizer\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tFood and Wood\"

u\"\\tOnce Synthetic Fertilizer is researched, you may build Hydroponic Farms. Hydroponic Farms raise much more food and wood than a normal Farm. These buildings take up four squares in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat it Produces\\n\\tFood in an Ocean Territory\"

u\"\\tOnce Advanced Structures has been developed you may build a Sea Platform. A Kelp Farm is built on a Sea Platform. Kelp Farms produce as much food as a Hydroponic Farm. Unlike other farms, they do not produce wood. These buildings take up one square on your Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tFood Replication\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tFood and Wood\"
u\"\\tFood Replicators produce much more food and wood than a Hydroponic Farm. Researching Food Replication lets you create these buildings. Food Replicators take up one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tIron and Endurium\"

u\"\\tSurface Mines produce iron and endurium. You cannot mine endurium until you research Endurium Mining. Surface Mines do best when placed in a mountainous territory or on rocky soil. They take up four squares.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tMolecular Bonding\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tIron and Endurium\"

u\"\\tThis building drills beneath the crust to mine a planet's molten rock. It then sucks molten iron and endurium to the surface where these metals cool down. It produces significantly more metal than a Surface Mine. These buildings take up one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tSub-Space Scanner\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tIron and Endurium\"

u\"\\tTapping into sub-space regions, this mine selectively pulls the atoms needed to create iron and endurium. It produces metal faster than a Mantle Drill. A Sub-Space Magnet only mines iron until Endurium Mining is researched. These buildings occupy one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tEnergy and Anti-Matter Pods\"

u\"\\tThese buildings generate energy for your colony. Swamps and cracked earth squares are ideal spots for Nuclear Plants. Also placing a Nuclear Plant over an energy bonus square produces much power. These buildings use up one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNuclear Fusion\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tEnergy and Anti-Matter Pods\"

u\"\\tResearching Nuclear Fusion technology lets you build this high output power plant. Fusion Plants create more energy than a Nuclear Plant. They generate even more power in swamps, cracked earth, or energy bonus squares. These buildings use one square on the settlement map.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAnti-Matter Containment\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tEnergy and Anti-Matter Pods\"

u\"\\tThis power plant generates energy by the controlled reaction of matter with anti-matter. Researching Anti-Matter Containment lets you construct this high energy producing plant. These buildings take up one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tEnergy and Anti-Matter Pods\"

u\"\\tThese plants use ocean currents to cleanly generate power. Once you have a Sea Platform, you may construct these efficient buildings. They produce as much energy as a Fusion Plant. These buildings take up one square on your Sea Platform.\"

u\"\\tFactories build both infantry and artillery units. They also convert iron into steel and endurium into triidium, once you research Metallurgy and Triidium Processing. Factories can also trade, giving you extra money. These buildings take up four squares in your settlement.\"

u\"\\tAutomation technology speeds up production, letting you build the faster Automated Factory.  Automated Factories make steel, triidium, and military units much faster than a Factory. Trade income is also increased. These buildings take up one square on your settlement map.\"

u\"\\tMetal Replication technology lets you build a Metal Replication Station. This advanced plant duplicates metallic components at a greatly accelerated rate. This process increases unit and resource production while using fewer colonists.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Medicines\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tPrevents Plagues\\n\\tHeals Injured Militia\"

u\"\\tHospitals are possible when you have Advanced Medicine technology. Hospitals prevent plagues effecting colonists and heal injured militia units. Their construction also lends a morale bonus to the territory. Note that Hospitals cannot stop a crop plague. These buildings use one square in your settlement.\"

u\"\\tShipyards can only be built on coastal territories. Key trading centers, they generate a lot of money. Shipyards also manufacture Sea Transports and warships. These buildings take up one square on your settlement map.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tShockwave Projectors\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tShip Units\\n\\tTrade\"

u\"\\tResearch Shockwave Projectors technology to build the high tech Hydroport. This dock manufactures ships quickly but creates less trade income than a Shipyard. Hydroports may only be built on coastal territories. These buildings take up one square in your settlement.\"

u\"\\tAirports give you trade income and also build airplanes. At first you can build the Turbo Wing Fighter. Research Starflare Bombs and Cloaking to build better airplanes. Airports also refuel aircraft. These buildings take up four squares in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNeutrionic Fuel\\n\\nWhat It Produce\\n\\tTrade\\n\\tAirplane Units\"

u\"\\tHigh octane Neutrionic Fuel lets you build the Military Airbase. These bases manufacture airplanes much faster than an Airport. Military Airbases also give you trade income. These buildings take up four squares on your settlement map.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNeutrionic Fuel\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tIncreases Range of Ground Units\\n\\tRefuels Airplanes\"

u\"\\tFuel Depots can increase the range of aircraft, infantry, and artillery units. Artillery and infantry units that enter Fuel Depot territories can move another territory that turn. These buildings use one square in a settlement.\"

u\"\\tCulture Centers raise morale by producing culture. Each culture point counters one point of bad morale. These buildings are great places for your weary colonists to unwind. They can be upgraded into the more efficient Museums. These buildings only use one square in your settlement.\"

u\"\\tMuseums are more relaxing places than Culture Centers, giving you even more culture. They cannot be built; only by upgrading a Culture Center can a Museum be made. These buildings use one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tEndurium Mining\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tCreates Art Objects\"

u\"\\tArt objects can only be made in Art Complexes. Every turn there is a chance of creating an art object. Each art object increases morale by two points; you can also sell an art object for a high price. These buildings take up four squares in your settlement.\"

u\"\\tLaser Defense fortifications strengthen your colony's resistance to invading forces. These rapid fire guns are about equal in power to a Laser Cannon. These buildings take up one square on your settlement map.\"

u\"\\tA Flak Launcher fires shrapnel into the path of air units.  This shrapnel is very effective at bringing down enemy missiles and aircraft. They can be built either on land or Sea Platforms. These buildings use up one square.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat it Does\\n\\tDefends Sea Platform Colonies\"
u\"\\tThis specialized defensive fortification damages enemy ships. These forts are essential to defending ocean settlements, using up one square on your Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tEnergy Deflectors\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDefends Colony\"

u\"\\tAn Energy Defense system is almost as effective as a Fusion Cannon. Once you finish Energy Deflector technology, put these powerful defense guns in place. These buildings take up one square on your settlement map.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAnti-Matter Deflectors\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDefends Colony\"

u\"\\tAnti-Matter Defense fortifications are the most powerful stationary guns you can build. This is a must for defense against Disruptor Cannon. Researching Anti-Matter Deflectors gives you this defensive system. These buildings take up one square in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tVortex Emitter\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDefends Sea Platforms from Ship Attack\"

u\"\\tThis Sea Platform device controls the water currents in all adjacent ocean territories. This damages all enemy ships in these territories. If a friendly sea unit is in an adjoining territory, no ships will be sunk. These buildings take up one square.\"

u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tMesotronic Generator\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDefends Sea Platforms from Air Attack\\n\\tAdds to Farm Production in Friendly Territories\\n\\tBlocks Orbital Surveillance\\n\\tCauses Floods in Enemy Territories\"

u\"\\tWeather Control Stations cause several different things to happen in adjacent territories. They cause enemy aircraft to crash, increase food production in adjacent friendly territories, cause floods in enemy territories, and block Orbital Surveillance technology. Enemy air units will not crash if they are in the same territory as a friendly air unit. These buildings take up one square on your Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tRocketry\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tBuilds Missile Units\"

u\"\\tBuild a Missile Base once you research Rocketry. Missile Bases manufacture all missile units - the Scatterpack, the Groundbreaker, and the Supernova Warheads. Research Ion Weapons and Anti-Matter Beams to get the more advanced missiles. These buildings take up one square in either a land settlement or a Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tOrbital Surveillance Systems\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tIncreases World Surveillance\\n\\tBuilds Missile Units\"

u\"\\tResearch Orbital Surveillance Systems and you can build these devastating silos. These buildings manufacture warheads much faster than a Missile Base. Also Anti-Colony Assault Systems launch surveillance satellites – improving what you can see in the Planet View. These buildings take up one square in either a land settlement or a Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tResearches Technology\\n\\tMakes Electronic Parts\"

u\"\\tOnce you build a University you can begin researching technologies. Also when you gain the Electronics technology, Universities can manufacture electronic parts for you. These large research centers take up four squares in a settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tChaos Computers\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tResearches Technology\\n\\tMakes Electronic Parts\"

u\"\\tThanks to Chaos Computer technology, these labs can do research faster and produce more electronic parts than a University. These buildings take up one square on your settlement map or Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tCortex Scanner\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tResearches Technology\\n\\tMakes Electronic Parts\"

u\"\\tCortex Scanner technology lets scientists communicate mentally, saving much time. Collective Tech Labs research technologies at a faster rate than a Tech Lab. The improved research facility allows scientists to make electronic parts quickly as well. These buildings take up one square in your settlement or Sea Platform.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tGives Idle Troops Combat Experience\"

u\"\\tMilitary Training Centers allow land and air units in a territory and sea units next to this territory to use the Train mission. These units then gain combat experience. Units can be trained up to Veteran status. A unit may only become Elite through combat experience. These buildings take up four squares in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tImproves Culture and Trade\\n\\tMakes Colonizers\\n\\tMakes Scouts\\n\\tMakes Command Corps\"

u\"\\tCity Centers are hubs of trade income and culture. A City Center builds Colonizers - units that move colonists into other territories. Once Electronics is researched, City Centers make Scouts and Command Corps units. When Advanced Medicine is studied, City Centers can also produce Medics. These buildings take up four squares in your settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Produces\\n\\tCulture and Research\"

u\"\\tThese ancient shrines may be found on various planets within the Dark Cloud. Remnants of an ancient civilization, these buildings are sought out by every race as places of great learning. Destroying a Land Shrine violates the Xythra Accord, so these buildings should be treated with great care. Land Shrines take up four squares.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat it Does\\n\\tA Random Resource Task\"

u\"\\tUnlike Land Shrines, Hidden Shrines cannot be detected without exploring a territory with land units or flying overhead with an Air Command plane. Smaller than Land Shrines, Hidden Shrines produce one resource; what resource this will be is chosen randomly. These buildings take up one square.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tA Random Resource Task\"

u\"\\tMuch like Hidden Shrines, these units can only be discovered by an Attack Submarine, Sea Command, or a Sea Platform. Building a Sea Platform in an Underwater Shrine's territory is the only way your colonists can work in these special buildings. Since these buildings are in the water, they do not use up any settlement squares.\"
u\"When It Appears\\n\\tWhen You Right Click on a Building\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\t Lets You Change a Building's Production\"

u\"\\tThis window lets you change a building's tasks, order new units to be manufactured, and even shut the building down. Each building has different task buttons that your colonists can work on. There is also a Housing Pool button that is not a task; this button tells you how many idle colonists you have in your settlement. Click and drag the colonists between all these task buttons to choose what you want the building to produce.\"
u\"Where It Appears\\n\\tAt The Bottom of the Building Properties Box\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tShows All the Colonists Working on a Selected Task\"

u\"\\tWhen a building's task button is selected, the Labor Pool at the bottom of the screen fills up with that task's colonists. These colonists can then be either clicked or dragged onto other tasks. They can also be placed on the Satellite View.\"
u\"What They Do\\n\\tLets You Change What Your Buildings Produce\"

u\"Right click a building to see its task buttons. Each button has a Dropzone where colonists may be placed upon or taken away, an Active area which displays the task's workers in the Labor Pool below, a Lock which prevents colonists from being added or removed from this task, and a Priority switch that makes all new colonists work on this task. Colonists may be clicked and dragged between all the building's task buttons.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tLets You Continuously Build One or a Set of Units\"

u\"\\tCity Centers, Factories, Shipyards, Airports, and Missile Bases manufacture military units. You can set up a circular queue so that the building will keep making the same unit or units over and over again. Select the units you wish to build and then check circular queue in the Building Properties Box. When the building has finished manufacturing the unit or units, it will start the queue all over again.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tIncreases a Building's Production\"

u\"\\tAdding colonists to a building increases its production. For instance, if a farm has two colonists on it, the building may produce 6 food and 1 wood. If you add more colonists the building, you might increase production to 9 food and 2 wood.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nMade from a Settlement's Population\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tNone\"

u\"\\tYour colonists carry small laser pistols. When an invading army attempts to take over your territory, your colonists will help you fight off the invaders. A single Militia represents 100 armed colonists. If the Militia is killed the colonists are killed.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone for Basic Colonizer\\tLater Uses Proximity Detectors\\n\\nMade in a City Center\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tBuild Settlement\\n\\tLay Mines\"

u\"\\tTerritories can only be settled by Colonizers. Start a settlement by moving your Colonizer onto a neutral territory. Right click your Colonizer in the Army Window to choose the Build Settlement mission. Next turn the settlement is yours. Once you develop Proximity Detector technology, your Colonizers will also have the Lay Mines mission.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Structures\\n\\nMade in a Shipyard\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tBuild Settlement\"

u\"\\tSea Platform Builders let colonists start settlements in coastal oceans. Start a settlement by moving your Sea Platform Builder into a neutral ocean territory. Right click on your Sea Platform Builder in the Army Window to choose the Build Settlement mission. Next turn your Sea Platform Builder will create a Sea Platform.\"

u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tElectronics\\n\\nMade in a City Center\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tSpy\\n\\tDisarm Mines\\n\\tSteal Technology\\n\\tSteal Resources (ChCh-t)\\n\\tSabotage Units (Maug)\\n\\tSubvert Morale (Re'Lu)\\n\\tPoison Land (Cyth)\"

u\"\\tAlthough they are poor in combat, Scouts have several special missions only they can do. All Scouts can spy, steal technology, and disarm mines. Some races also have special missions that let Scouts steal resources, sabotage units, subvert morale, and poison land.\"

u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tElectronics\\n\\nMade in a City Center\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tGives Ground Units an Attack Bonus\\n\\tMind Blast (Cyth)\\n\\tMind Control (Re'Lu)\\n\\tShaman Dance (Uva Mosk)\"

u\"\\tCommand Corps units give all artillery and infantry units in their territory a better chance to hit their targets. The Cyth Corps have a special Mind Blast attack. Re'Lu Corps Mind Control enemy units – forcing them to fight for the Re'Lu. Uva Mosk Corps create new resources in territories with their Shaman Dance mission.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tSpy (Uva Mosk)\\n\\tBerserk (Humans)\\n\\tJuggernaut (Tarth)\"

u\"\\tYou can build Laser Squads in any Factory. Human infantry may be ordered to go Berserk – which gives them a combat bonus but kills them after the battle. Tarth units can Juggernaut, letting them easily destroy enemy buildings. Uva Mosk infantry can Spy in a rival territory.\"

u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tSurface-to-Air Missiles\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tCan Take Out Aircraft And Missiles\\n\\tSpy (Uva Mosk)\\n\\tBerserk (Humans)\\n\\tJuggernaut (Tarth)\"

u\"\\tSAM Troopers are equipped with missiles that attack both ground and air targets. Thus SAM Troopers can be used against artillery, infantry, airplanes, and missiles. The Humans, Uva Mosk, and Tarth SAM Troopers all have special combat abilities.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAnti-Matter Rifles\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tSpy (Uva Mosk)\\n\\tBerserk (Humans)\\n\\tJuggernaut (Tarth)\"

u\"\\tBattle Troopers have strong defensive and offensive abilities. Once you have Anti-Matter Rifle technology, Battle Troopers are available in your factories. The Humans, Uva Mosk, and Tarth Battle Troopers all have special combat abilities.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAssault Armor\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tSpy (Uva Mosk)\\n\\tBerserk (Humans)\\n\\tJuggernaut (Tarth)\"

u\"\\tAssault Troopers are the strongest infantry unit you can put on the battlefield. Research Assault Armor to outfit these troops. The Human, Uva Mosk, and Tarth Assault Troopers all have special combat abilities.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Medicine\\n\\nMade in a City Center\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tHeals Injured Ground Units\"

u\"\\tMedics reduce damage to infantry units during combat. If a Medic dies during a battle, these advantages cease. You may build Medics in a City Center after you have researched Advanced Medicine.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Medicine\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tHeals Injured Ground Units\"
u\"\\tFactories manufacture Laser Tanks. These tanks are armed with a large version of the laser rifle, shooting a penetrating beam that burns buildings and maims Laser Squads.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tFusion Cannon\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tNone\"

u\"\\tResearch Fusion Cannon to manufacture these strong artillery units. They create a beam by fusing atoms together and projecting the resulting energy. Fusion Cannon are especially good at taking out Laser Defense installations.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tFusion Cannon\\n\\nMade in a Shipyard\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tMoves Over Both Ground and Water\"
u\"\\tAn Amphibious Assault Vehicle (AAV) moves on land or water. They are about as powerful as a Fusion Cannon.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tDisruptor Beams\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tNone\"

u\"\\tMore effective than Fusion Cannon,  Disruptor Cannon fire an encased projectile of anti-matter. When this projectile impacts a target, the anti-matter is released. Any matter in its range instantly explodes. They are great for taking out Energy Defense installations.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAnti-Matter Beams\\n\\nMade in a Factory\\n\\nSpecial Missions\\n\\tNone\"

u\"\\tThe most destructive mobile gun in the galaxy, the Holocaust Cannon releases a disintegrating anti-matter beam. Research Anti-Matter Beam technology to make these units in your factories. They destroy Anti-Matter Defense installations with ease.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nMade in an Airport\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tGood at Destroying Other Air Units\"

u\"\\tThese airplanes are armed with efficient air-to-air weapons systems, so they are also great defense against Starflare Bombers and Supernova Spyjets. They also can attack ground targets - but with less success.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tStarflare Bombs\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tCan Fight Ships and Ground Units\"

u\"\\tResearch Starflare Bomb technology to make these powerful airplanes. These aircraft are devastating against stationary ground targets. Starflare Bombers get their name because they use bombs that explode with eye searing intensity.\"

u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nMade in Airports\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tIncreases Air Unit Accuracy\\n\\tProvides Improved Visibility\\n\\tCan Detect Hidden Shrines\\n\\tCan Uncloak Hidden Units\"

u\"\\tAir Command units are an aerial center of command. They give all air units a combat bonus in a territory and can spy on surrounding territories. Due to their advanced scanning systems, they can detect Hidden Shrines from the air, and they can also perform the Uncloak Mission, allowing them to reveal an enemy's cloaked units.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tCloaking\\n\\nMade in Airports\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tExcellent Against Air and Ground Targets\\n\\tSpy Mission\"

u\"\\tCloaking technology gives you this incredible attack plane. Deadly against both air and ground targets, a Supernova Spyjet can also spy like a Scout. They are the most powerful air unit you can build.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tNone\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tMoves Units Over Oceans\\n\\tCan Attack Ships and Airplanes\\n\\tLays Mines\"

u\"\\tSea Transports haul up to three land units across ocean territories. Colonizers, Scouts, Command Corps, Infantry, and Artillery units may all be moved by these ships. Once Proximity Detector technology is researched, these units can be set to the Lay Mines mission. When set to this mission, the Sea Transport disbands, leaving behind several deadly underwater mines.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tUnderwater Tracking\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tUnderwater Search\"

u\"\\t Destroyers are excellent at taking out submarines, having double the chance to hit them, compared to any other naval unit. When given the Underwater Search mission they have a good chance of discovering hidden subs.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tShockwave Projectors\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tCan Attack Ships and Airplanes\"

u\"\\tShockwave Dreadnoughts unleash a harsh sonic wave that shakes apart enemy ships, causing them to sink. The shockwave also shakes loose the wings on bombing aircraft. This is the most heavily armed ship you can build.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tZero Friction Hulls\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tSilent Running\\n\\tHunt\\n\\tDisarm Mines\"

u\"\\tZero Friction Hull technology lets you build Attack Submarines. These underwater vessels are excellent for spying. When set to the Hunt mission, they can ambush unsuspecting ship units. Attack Submarines are also good at finding hidden Undersea Shrines, and they are the only naval unit that can perform the Disarm Mines mission.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tIon Weapons\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tAttacks Ships And Airplanes\\n\\tRefuels Friendly Airplanes\"

u\"\\tThe Shockwave Carrier transports refuels airplanes. Any aircraft within range of a Shockwave Carrier will not crash at the end of a turn. These ships are a convenient way to increase the range of your air units.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tFlak\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tAttacks Airplanes and Missiles\"
u\"\\tThis specially designed ship is basically a floating defense system. Pairing this unit with a Sea Command will let you take out many air units.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tElectronics\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tImproves Accuracy of Friendly Sea Units\\n\\tLocates Sea Shrines\"

u\"\\tThese ships have impressive sensors that gather many details on a battle. Sea Command ships improve the targeting ability of all friendly sea units in the territory. The Sea Command also has a good probability of discovering any Undersea Shrines it passes over.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tRocketry\\n\\nMade in Shipyards\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\attacks Coastal Land Territories\"

u\"\\tThese impressive ships bombard coastal territories. The missile it uses is not quite as powerful as a Scatterpack Warhead. However, since this sea unit is mobile, it can help you devastate territories that are out of your normal missile range.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tRocketry\\n\\nMade in a Missile Base\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tAttacks at Long Range\"
u\"\\tOnce a Missile Base is finished, you can build these warheads. They are excellent for softening up the defensive systems on a rival settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tIon Weapons\\n\\nMade in Missile Bases\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tAttack Ships and Settlements at a Long Range\"
u\"\\tOnce a Missile Base is finished, you can build these warheads. They are excellent for softening up the defensive systems on a rival settlement.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAnti-Matter Beams\\n\\nMade in Missile Bases\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tCan Attack Settlements At Long Range\"
u\"\\tThe most destructive weapon known in existence. Once Anti-Matter Beams are researched your missile bases can make Supernova Warheads - and your enemies had better beware!\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tProximity Detectors\\n\\nMade by Colonizers and Sea Transports\\n\\nSpecial Abilities\\n\\tNone\"

u\"\\tMinefields are invisible defenses that can be placed in land or sea territories. These mines explode when approached by enemy armor, infantry, or ships units, causing catastrophic damage to these units. They are planted on land by Colonizers and planted at sea by Sea Transports. Researching Proximity Dectectors gives these units the lay mines mission.\"
u\"What Happens\\n\\tUnits get combat advantages as they gain experience\"

u\"\\tIf a unit survives a battle, it gains combat experience. Experience can also be earned at a Military Training Center using the Train mission. More experienced units attack and defend themselves better. There are three levels of experience - green, veteran, and elite.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\t All Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tOnly Attacks Other Units\"
u\"\\tWhen given this order, the unit only attacks enemy units and does not damage buildings. This is the starting default order for most units.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tAttacks Nearest Target\"
u\"\\tThis order tells the unit to attack the nearest target - either a military unit or a building.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tAttacks Buildings\"
u\"\\tThis command orders the unit to destroy all buildings in a territory first. This lets you slow down your rival's development.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tUnit Stays Away From Heavy Combat\"
u\"\\tUse this order to keep your command units and Medics out of a battle. This way they will not be destroyed and their special abilities will help out your main forces.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tTarth Infantry Only\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tDestroys Buildings \"
u\"\\tTarth infantry are especially good at destroying buildings. When they are given this order they ram into a building repeatedly until it falls down.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units Except Aircraft\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tCuts Combat Speed in Half\\n\\tReduces Chance Hitting Mines\"
u\"\\tAny unit set to this mission dramatically reduces its chance being damaged by a mine. However a unit's combat speed is also cut in half.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tSpies and Submarines\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tFinds and Eliminates Mines\"

u\"\\tUnits given this mission will attempt to diffuse the mines in the assigned territory. This is carried out like any other Submarine or Scout mission, with a chance for success each turn. If successful, the whole minefield is disabled. Scouts and Submarines carry out this mission in their \\\"cloaked\\\" modes.  As a result, there are three different ways in which the mission may fail. The most common is that the unit does not disable the mine and nothing else occurs. The other two possibilities are that the unit will be discovered as a spy and eliminated or that the unit will accidentally detonate a mine and be destroyed.\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tGets Units Off a Battlefield\"

u\"\\tAll units, except Berserk and Mind Controlled units, may flee a battle. Set your unit to Retreat when a percentage of its defense points are gone. A unit with 4 defense points set to 50% retreat will flee a battle when it takes 2 points of damage.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tNeutral Mode \"
u\"\\tUnits given this command do no special mission.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tCatches Spies\"

u\"\\tPatrolling units detect spying Scouts - immediately destroying them. If a patrolling unit moves to another territory it cannot look for spies until the next turn. Patrolling units lower morale.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tScouts\\n\\tSpyjets\\n\\tUva Mosk Infantry\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tMakes The Territory Visible To You\"

u\"\\tScouts can slip across enemy borders to spy. Click and drag the unit into the rival territory. If the mission succeeds you can see into that territory next turn. Your spy could be caught if your rival has units set on the Patrol mission.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tGives Unit to Another Colony\"
u\"\\tThis mission lets you give the unit to another colony. Select the Transfer To... mission that has your ally's name on it. The next turn the unit become theirs.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tScouts\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tTakes a Technology From Another Colony\"

u\"\\tSend a Scout into an enemy colony with this dangerous mission and you might get a technology for free! Note that most Scouts are more easily caught doing this mission, however Maug Scouts have less chance of being captured.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tFixes the Unit's Battle Damage\"
u\"\\tThis mission repairs all damage done to the unit. When a unit is set to Repair it cannot move or fight during that turn. The next turn it will be back to full strength.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tGives The Unit Combat Experience\"

u\"\\tThis mission allows idle units to gain combat experience. The Training mission is only available to land and air units that are in a territory with a Military Training Center. Sea units may also train in these centers if they are in an nearby ocean territory. Units may be trained up to one point below elite status. Elite status can only be achieved on the battlefield.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAttack Submarines\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tGathers Information\"
u\"\\tSubmarines set on Silent Running are hidden from your opponents. They also avoid combat.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAttack Submarines\\n\\tEffect\\n\\tSurprise attack\"
u\"\\tSubmarines set on Hunt prowl beneath the water's surface until they see an enemy unit. Then the sub surfaces and ambushes the unit.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tDestroyers\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tSearch And Destroy Enemy Subs\"
