u\"\\tThis mission sets your Destroyer on submarine patrol, scanning the sea floor. When discovered, Attack Submarines are forced to the surface to fight.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tAll Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tForces Unhappy Colonists Back to Work\"

u\"\\tThis mission imposes martial law on a territory, forcing irate colonists back to work. This helps when you are taxing your colonists heavily. If a suppressing unit is moved to another territory, it cannot suppress until the next turn.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tRe'Lu Scouts\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tLowers Morale in Territory\"

u\"\\tOnly Re'Lu Scouts have this special mission. Using their telepathic powers, Re'Lu mentally manipulate colonists to rebel against their colony. Colonist morale is hurt each turn the subverting Scout is in that territory.\"
u\"Special Ability\\n\\nPossessed By\\n\\tRe'Lu Command Corps\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tTakes Over Enemy Units During Combat\"

u\"\\tRe'Lu Command Corps units have this special innate power. During a battle there is a chance that an opposing unit will fall under the telepathic control of a Re'Lu Command Corps. This unit then turns against its colony and then fights for the Re'Lu - forever!\"
u\"Order\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tHuman Infantry Units\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tIncreases Attack Strength\"

u\"\\tOnly Human infantry units have this special attack. These troops inject themselves with a toxic adrenaline that gives them a huge attack bonus. However this adrenaline is fatal. All berserk units die after the battle.\"
u\"Special Ability\\n\\nPossessed By\\n\\tCyth Command Corps\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tKills Enemy Units\"

u\"\\tOnly Cyth Command Corps units have this innate ability. By focusing a blast of psionic energy, they scramble the brains of whomever opposes them. These mind blasted units are quickly destroyed. Note that this is an ability, not a mission.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tMaug Scouts\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tDestroys Artillery, Airplanes, and Missiles\"

u\"\\tMaug Scouts can quickly reprogram enemy artillery and aircraft computers, causing them to self-destruct. They can also manipulate missile guidance systems - forcing missiles to go off and target their own territories! If the territory has no units the Scout does damage to a building.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tChCh-t Scouts\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tSteals Resources From Enemy\"
u\"\\tChCh-t Scouts can sneak across enemy borders to steal resources. They find whatever resource is the most plentiful and then take all of it!\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tCyth Scouts\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tCauses Crop Plague\"
u\"\\tCyth Scouts set to this mission infect an enemy's land with a disease. This causes a crop plague that destroys half the food in that territory.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nPossessed By\\n\\tUva Mosk Command Corps Only\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tCreates Resource Bonus\"
u\"\\tThe Shaman mission gives Uva Mosk Command Corps units a chance to create a resource bonus square in a territory. They can create resource bonus squares for food, iron, endurium, and energy.\"
u\"Mission\\n\\nCan Be Given To\\n\\tColonizers\\n\\tSea Transports\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tCreates a Minefield\"

u\"\\tOnce you have researched Proximity Detectors, Colonizers and Sea Transports can be set to create Minefields. Once the mines are laid, the unit is disbanded. Enemy units that then enter this territory have a high chance of being destroyed. Scouts and Submarines have a Disarm Mines mission, letting them dismantle minefields.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tChanges an AI Controlled Colony's Attitude Towards You\\n\\tHelps or Hinders Pact Creation\\n\\nWhen It Happens\\n\\tWhenever You Do Something to an AI Controlled Colony\"

u\"\\tNon-player races keep track of their feelings towards you. Based your race's past history, they may like you or hate you at the beginning of a game. Any actions performed later which affect the computer controlled race will change their feelings towards you. The more they like you, the better your chances are of forging a pact. The less they like you, the higher the chance is that they start a war with you.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tOffers Other Players to Join a Pact\\n\\nWhen It Happens\\n\\tUse the Pacts Button\"

u\"\\tThe Pacts button displays all the different treaties you can propose. You can also break existing pacts from this screen. Once a pact is proposed, the targeted player may accept or decline your offer.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tBreaks An Existing Pact\\n\\nWhen It Happens\\n\\tUse the Pacts Button\"

u\"\\tPacts can either be broken diplomatically or sneakily. Back-stabbing a pact member gives you a brief advantage, but creates an enemy. Announcing a break removes any chance of a surprise advantage. However, it does end the alliance on better terms.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tShows All Existing Pacts\\n\\nWhen It Happens\\n\\tWhen You Use The Pacts Button\"

u\"\\tEnter the Pacts screen to see what treaties have been made between which players. All pacts are shown by their type and their status. A pact's status will be one of these states - Proposed, Inactive, Active, Backstabbed, or Broken.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tPrevents Members from Accidentally Fighting\"

u\"\\tWhen you enter this pact, you are not allowed to enter a neutral territory at the same time your ally does. If this occurs, both forces are bounced back to their previous positions. You are also restricted from entering an ally's own territory. In both cases, you can move into the desired territory if you first break the Non-Aggression Pact.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tMembers May Travel Within Each Other's Territories\"

u\"\\tThis pact lets you enter most territories owned by your ally. Only territories with City Centers cannot be occupied by you. Military Pact partners never attack one another when they are in the same territory. If both enter an enemy territory, they will fight together.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tAllies Share Technology Development\"

u\"\\tPlayers jointly research technologies, sharing their discoveries with each other. A pact partner gains a new technology at the end of a turn. Colonies do not share any technologies that were researched before the pact was made. These allies also do not share discoveries made from other technology pacts.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tYou Can See All Your Ally Sees\"

u\"\\tAllies who agree to this pact can see everything the other colony sees. However, allies can not see what changes their ally is making during a turn. They must wait until the start of the next turn to see the new changes.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tYou Share the Victory!\"

u\"\\tThis pact joins your two colonies together. You share the victory conditions and gain all the benefits from the Military, Technology, and Intelligence Pacts. Unlike a Military Pact, Victory Pact members can enter territories that have City Centers in them. If one victory pact member meets the victory conditions, they both win. Note that City Centers or captured Shrines do not add up between both players. Each ally must reach these victory conditions on their own. They still, however, share the victory.\"
u\"How To Activate\\n\\tDrag and Drop Resources Between Territories\\n\\tUse the Trade Button\"

u\"\\tStart a trade by clicking and dragging a resource to another colony. You can click and drag resources from either from the Planet View or the Resource Bar. Set the price and the amount of resources you wish to sell - then wait to find out if the colony accepts your deal or not.\"
u\"How To Activate\\n\\tRight Click a Unit in the Army Window and Select the Transfer Mission\"

u\"\\tEvery unit has several Transfer To... missions.  This lets you give the unit to another colony. Right click a unit in the Army Window to see its Unit Status screen. Select the race to whom you wish to give the unit. Next turn it will join that colony.\"
u\"How To Activate\\n\\tUse the Send Message Button\"

u\"\\tSend insults, brags, threats, complaints, compliments, and your own personal messages to your opponents. Click on the send message button. Choose from the available animated messages. You may also select custom to write your own. Remember, sending nasty messages to computer controlled opponents will make them mistrust you... so be careful what you say.\"

u\"\\tA territory may become stricken with a plague, killing off significant numbers of a territory's population. The plague can spread to other territories by moving resources and colonists out of the afflicted settlement. Hospitals cure and prevent the outbreak of plagues.\"

u\"\\tOccasionally an unknown disease kills off your crops. Territories afflicted with a crop plague lose half of their food. Moving infected food to other parts of your colony might spread the crop plague to other territories.\"

u\"\\tIf your colony's morale is high, your colonists may throw a large celebration in your honor! During this party they hold a special fund raising campaign, donating many credits to your treasury.\"
u\"Cause\\n\\tChance Event\\n\\nEffect\\n\\tGives You Resource Bonus Square\"

u\"\\tOccasionally your colonists may discover a mother lode of iron or a fertile patch of soil they missed in their first scan. Place the appropriate building over the bonus square and send your production soaring!\"

u\"\\tOn many Shrine worlds, natives spend much of their time watching all the colonies. If your morale is high there is a strong chance that some natives will join your colony - adding to your population.\"
u\"\\tAn earthquake may strike at any time, damaging buildings and killing colonists.\"
u\"\\tWeather Control Stations can direct torrential rains down on enemy settlements. This causes flash floods, inflicting great damage.\"

u\"\\tThe upper atmosphere is occasionally besieged by ion storms. These storms disrupt Orbital Surveillance System technology, causing these satellites to not work for a while. This makes it harder to see details in the Planet View.\"
u\"How To Contact the Skirineen\\n\\tUse the Black Market Button\\n\\nWhat They Do\\n\\tBuy and Sell Resources\\n\\tSell Military Units, Resources, Information, and Technologies\"

u\"\\tThe Skirineen are despised by all races because of their past aggression during the Skirineen Conquest. When you contact the Skirineen they will not respond immediately -- sometimes not at all! They may reply to you as quickly as one turn or take as long as five turns. The Skirineen have their own schedule and you just may not be on it.\"

u\"\\tEven though your meetings with the Skirineen are done in secret, there is a chance that your colonists will discover your transgression. If your dealings are revealed, there will be a scandal in your colony – lowering morale. If you abuse your relationship with the Skirineen, this morale penalty will become much more severe.\"
u\"Risk Involved - Low\\n\\tMorale Penalty If Caught - Minor\"

u\"\\tThe Skirineen have several resources you can purchase. If you are low on a resource consider buying it from them. They also pay a nice price for any resources you might want to sell. The chances of these transactions causing a scandal are low.\"
u\"Risk Involved - Medium\\n\\tMorale Penalty If Caught - Moderate\"

u\"\\tCatch up on a more advanced neighbor by buying a technology from the Skirineen. Note that sometimes the Skirineen might not have a technology to sell. There is a medium chance that your colonists will catch you buying technology from the Skirineen.\"
u\"Risk Involved - High\\n\\tMorale Penalty If Caught - Major\"

u\"\\tThe Skirineen have special surveillance satellites which let them see the entire planet. Pay their price and you can directly view a rival territory. This can be a very wise move when you are looking for shrines. Note that the chances of a scandal are high.\"
u\"Risk Involved - High\\n\\tMorale Penalty If Caught - Severe\"

u\"\\tEach turn the Skirineen have different units available. Some may even be at a higher technology than what you can manufacture. This is a great way to even the odds in a lopsided battle. There is a high possibility that your colonists will find out though. If they do, a major scandal will erupt!\"

u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tColonists Grow Quickly\\n\\tChCh-t Housing Holds Double Colonists\\n\\tBuild Buildings at 120% Rate\\n\\tProduce All Units at 110% Rate\\n\\tUnits Move Faster\\n\\tScouts Steal Resources\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tPoor Researchers\"

u\"\\tThe ChCh-t rapidly reproduce their population. Because of their hive mentality, more ChCh-t colonists can also live inside one Housing building. They have weak military units, but these units do move quickly in combat. They also manufacture infantry units extremely fast. Their Scouts can steal resources from other colonies.\"

u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tCyth Scouts Can Poison Land\\n\\tCyth Command Corps Have Mind Blast Ability\\n\\tMorale Rarely Changes\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tPacts Difficult - Disliked by All Races\\n\\tCan Never Use Full Work Force\"

u\"\\tThe Cyth Command Corps has a special Mind Blast ability that mangles enemy units. Their Scouts can also Poison Land, which cuts a territory's food production in half. Cyth morale changes very little so Skirineen scandals do not hurt the Cyth population very much. Scandals do cause morale to drop - but rarely for longer than a turn.\"

u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tHave 130% of the Normal Trade Income\\n\\tReceive More Taxes Than Other Races\\n\\tHave Reduced Transport Costs\\n\\tInfantry Have Berserk Battle Order\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tMore Prone To Scandal\\n\\tCosts More To Maintain Large Military\"

u\"\\tHumans are a trade-based culture who make a lot of money each turn. Their infantry also have a special Berserk order. Berserk infantry attack with a huge combat bonus; however the infantry unit is destroyed at the end of the battle. Humans are highly prone to Skirineen scandals. Human military units also cost more to maintain.\"

u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tProduce Electronics And Military Units Faster\\n\\tScouts Sabotage Units and Steal Technologies\\n\\tResearch Faster\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tColonists Rebel More Often\\n\\tWeaker Infantry Units\"

u\"\\tThe Maug develop technologies quickly. Maug Scouts are adept at stealing technologies and sabotaging enemy artillery, airplanes, warheads, and buildings. Due to their ill health the Maug military is relatively weak. However, their rapid production of military units lets them create a military force quickly.\"
u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tSee More in Planet View\\n\\tCommand Corps Have Mind Control Ability\\n\\tScouts Have Subvert Mission\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tHave Weak Military Units\"

u\"\\tRe'Lu telepathy lets them see the entire Planet View without any Orbital Surveillance technology. Re'Lu Scouts have a special Subvert mission that hurts a territory's morale. Their Command Corps Mind Control enemy units, forcing them to fight for the Re'Lu. Any units captured this way fight until death for their new Re'Lu leaders.\"
u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tHave Strongest Military in the Galaxy\\n\\tProduce Food Quickly\\n\\tInfantry Have Juggernaut Order\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tTheir Ships Are Weak\\n\\tScouts Do Not Spy Well\"

u\"\\tThe Tarth have the strongest military known in the galaxy Their ground and air units have huge combat bonuses. Tarth infantry have a juggernaut order which destroys enemy buildings with ease. Their farmers also raise great quantities of food for their troops. Due to their immense size however, Tarth Scouts make poor spies. Tarth ships are not as strong as other races' fleets; they are often easily sunk.\"

u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tProduce More Natural Resources\\n\\tAll Infantry Units Can Spy\\n\\tCommand Corps Have Shaman Mission\\n\\tCan Maintain Large Military Forces With Lower Costs\\n\\tImproved Chance to Hit in Combat\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tCollect Little In Taxes\"

u\"\\tThe Uva Mosk produce more natural resources than any other race. Since they are patriotic revolutionaries, their military units cost less to maintain each turn. Their expertise at guerrilla warfare lets them train their units to hit better; also all Uva Mosk infantry units may spy. Their Command Corps units have a special Shaman mission which creates bonus squares on their territories. Fiercely independent, Uva Mosk colonists pay little in taxes.\"

u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tRun Black Market\\n\\tBuy and Sell Resources\\n\\tSell Technologies,  Military Units, and Information\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tDo Not Colonize\\n\\tCause Scandals In Colony\\n\\tAre Disliked By All - Even More That The Cyth!\"

u\"\\tMistrusted by all because of their violent past, the Skirineen lurk threateningly on the fringe of galactic civilization. A small group of Skirineen are currently trailing all expeditions into the Dark Cloud. They are mainly buying and selling resources, but they also have technologies, information, and military units for sale.\"
u\"ADVANTAGES:\\n\\tGives Information To You\\n\\nDISADVANTAGES:\\n\\tAlarmingly Small Gene Pool\"

u\"\\tBecause the Skirineen drove off or killed most of us Tolnans, we now travel with you into the Dark Cloud in the hope of finding survivors from our lost race. Since the signing of the Gallius IV Compact, we Tolnans have served as advisors to all colony leaders.\"
u\"What They Do\\n\\tAllows a Player to Choose Gameplay Advantages or Disadvantages\"

u\"\\tAvailable on the race selection screen, this option lets you choose advantages or disadvantages for your colony. This balances multiplayer games between novice and advanced players. Areas which may be changed include military strength, starting resources, and resource production.\"
u\"Defend Early and Place Your Defense Forts Intelligently\"

u\"\\t Build Laser Defense installations when you first land. This will protect you from an early surprise attack. As with any fort, building these in \\\"clumps\\\" lets them \\\"team up\\\" their attacks on invaders. Use mountain territories to your defensive advantage. In the mountains, you only need to defend two fronts against land attacks, since ground units can not attack from the \\\"mountainous side\\\" of a territory. This means you can stack your land defenses in those areas. Also, when mines are laid in mountain territories, they are only laid along the two open borders. This increases their concentration, making them twice as hard to avoid.\"
u\"Do not Fall Behind in Technology\"

u\"\\tBuild a University immediately. If your enemies get ahead in technology, they will not wait for you to catch up. Building multiple research centers, and upgrading them as soon as possible is a high priority. Also, form a technological strategy that compliments your game style. Keep in mind special world resource amounts when planning the order in which you research technologies. Food, for instance, may be more of an issue on some worlds, prompting you to research Synthetic Fertilizer before Fusion Cannon.\"
u\"Build Territories that are as Self Sufficient as Possible.\"

u\"\\tTeam buildings together that make and use complimentary resources. For instance, build a Factory with a Surface Mine. You should also have each settlement make as many resources as possible. This cuts down on transportation costs. Always build structures on squares rich with a specific resource. Press the <Insert> key in the Territory View to find out what each square produces. You can also right click a single square to see its resource potential. Finally, remember that multiple factories in a territory will allow for faster production of units. Three factories will build units three times as fast as one factory would.\"
u\"Attack with Missiles First, Then Launch a Land Unit Attack.\"

u\"\\tCombining a missile attack with a ground attack improves your chances to take over a territory. When you have Targeting Computers technology, you will be able to set your missiles to hit specific buildings. Missiles are also quite effective against sea units. Finally, a missile can be used as a rapid \\\"one-time-only\\\" scout, giving you a look at a territory that is currently out of range.\"
u\"Build or Destroy Housing Depending on What You Need\"

u\"\\tConstruct Housing when you need more colonists and destroy these buildings when you need less colonists. Housing eventually increases your population, but overpopulated territories lose morale. You will never need more than four Luxury Housing buildings per territory, though the ChCh-t need only two of these buildings. Transport colonists into new territories as soon as you can.  Territories that are 50-75% full of colonists grow the fastest, giving you much in both taxes and labor. Note that when colonists are transferred from one territory to another, their morale remains the same. Moving unhappy colonists to a new territory will lower that territory's morale.\"

u\"\\tAlways increase your food supply. As your colonists and military units grow, they will need a lot of food. Food keeps their morale high. It is best to keep food in reserve just in case their is a crop plague in your colony. Try to build farms in every territory in order to avoid shipping costs.\"
u\"Use All the Special Missions, Battle Orders, and Abilities That You Have\"

u\"\\tMake full use of any Scout and Command Corps special abilities that your race may have. For instance Re'Lu Scouts can subvert a territory's morale. This ability could let the Re'Lu get ahead in production. Uva Mosk Command Corps can create resource bonuses, improving your production.  Also, don't forget about the \\\"Patrol\\\" mission, which boosts your units' chances of discovering spies.\"

u\"\\tSome units only show their true colors when they are paired with a complementary unit. Starflare Bombers, for instance, are devastating against ground forces, but they have problems defending against air attacks. Pairing them with Turbo Wing Fighters, which are excellent in air-to-air combat, but cannot attack ground forces well, gives you a truly ruthless team. Also, try pairing a Flak Ship with a Siege Cruiser. This lets you bombard your opponents with missiles while defending against their inevitable missile-retaliation. Experiment with different combinations of units in order to come up with effective combinations\"

u\"\\tMany buildings need energy each turn or they shut down. More advanced buildings need more power, so your demand for energy will increase as you upgrade your settlement. Power plants built on cracked earth squares produce the most energy.\"

u\"\\tIsolating enemy troops from their colony weakens them as these units are cut off from their food supply. If a supply line is not set up again soon the military units eventually disband. If you cut off one enemy territory from another, these territories are unable to transport resources between themselves. This significantly slows down an enemy colony's production.\"
u\"\\tAll toolbar buttons either control some part of your colony or give you information. There are three ways to view your map - the Planet View, Territory View, and the Satellite View. \"

u\"\\tThe Colony Assistant lets you make changes to an entire territory from one screen. It groups all your buildings' separate tasks into a series of joined task buttons. The Colony Assistant is very helpful as your colony grows in size.\"

u\"\\tThe Event Log displays all new information on your colony. It automatically appears at the beginning of each turn. When you have not read an event it stays lit, when you have read an event it is darkened, and events that did not occur this turn are grayed-out.\"
u\"\\tYour units and colonists can be moved in several ways. Colonists can be moved between buildings or territories you own. Military units can move between most territories.\"

u\"\\tThese areas help or hurt your colony's growth. You must balance many things to keep your colonists happy while your increase resource production and manufacture military units. This is the key to maintaining a successful colony.\"
u\"\\tDifferent terrain types help or hinder your resource production. Choosing the best place to construct your buildings and settlements is essential to making your colony thrive.\"

u\"\\tFood, wood, iron, energy, and art objects can be produced without any special technologies. Steel, endurium, triidium, electronic parts, and anti-matter pods all require a specific technology in order to be made. Without enough resources, your colony can not survive. \"
u\"\\tYou cannot develop technologies until you build a University. Technological breakthroughs are necessary to create advanced resources, buildings, and military units.\"

u\"\\tChoose which buildings you want to construct with the Build button in the Territory View. While you are in the Planet View, this button is grayed out. At first you can only make buildings which produce little, but as your technologies improve and your resources grow, you can construct better buildings.\"

u\"\\tAll City Centers, Factories, Airports, Shipyards, and Missile Bases manufacture military units. When you first construct these buildings you may only make a few weak units. As these buildings advance, however, you can also make more powerful units. Use military units to expand and defend your colony.\"

u\"\\tRight click on a unit on the Army Window and the Unit Orders box appears. You can give a unit both a battle order and a mission. A battle order tells the unit how to fight. A mission gives the unit an overall task to perform, such as spying or stealing technology. Some units also have special innate abilities.\"
u\"\\tForm pacts with other races to improve your colony. By sending threatening messages to or trading with other colonies, these rivals could either become strong allies or bitter enemies.\"
u\"\\tThese are some events the planet may throw your way. Some are good. Some are bad. All of them could change your strategy in a hurry.\"

u\"\\tThe Skirineen are always looking to close a deal with you. Though they cannot participate in the quest for the Xythra, they still secretly follow colony ships, selling resources, technologies, military units, and information to all who need it. Deal with the Skirineen and you risk a scandal. Be warned that though they may seem nice, their only concern is to further their own shadowy goals.\"
u\"\\tEach race has special abilities and weaknesses. Find out more about yourself and your rivals to improve your strategy.\"
u\"\\tThere are many strategies you can use to defeat your rivals. Your overall plan depends on whether you need to build City Centers, claim Shrines, or destroy rival colonies.\"
u\"What It Does\\n\\tGives You Information\\n\\nHow to Get Help\\n\\nPress the Help Button\\n\\nWhen Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\tMost Subscreens\"
u\"This button lets you contact me, Oolan. I offer my help to all colony leaders. If you click the Help button, it brings up all my information, letting you to search for a desired topic.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Structures\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tAllows Buildings to Be Placed at Sea\"

u\"\\tThe product of a Sea Platform Builder, this structure allows you to place buildings in coastal sea territories. When created, it is furnished with a Sea Hab to house colonists. In addition, Sea Platforms may host Kelp Farms, Torpedo Launchers, Tidal Vortex Generators, Weather Control Stations, Flak Launchers, Tech and Collective Tech Labs, all Shipyards, Tidal Energy Plants, and all missile complex buildings.\"
u\"Technology Needed\\n\\tAdvanced Structures\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tHouses a Sea Platform's Population\"

u\"\\tSea Habs may not be build separately. They are an integral part of a Sea Platform, housing and sustaining the structure's population. Sea Habs hold up to 15 colonists and support them with Housing, Trade, and Culture tasks. ChCh-t Sea Habs hold up to 20 colonists.\"
u\"Use Your Diplomatic Skills to either Befriend or Offend Other Races.\"

u\"\\tThere are several ways in which you can influence another race's feelings towards you. First, you can use chats to either anger them (using Insult, Threat, and Brag), or make them like you (using Praise). Second, you can offer them pacts which, even if refused, can drive up other race's opinions of you. Third, you can trade with competing races. In so doing, you can make them like you more. Finally, and most significantly, you can gain a race's favor by attacking their enemies.\"
u\"Use Your Colonists Efficiently. Don't Apply Too Much Labor for the Job.\"

u\"\\tMake sure that you don't have any colonists performing unnecessary labor.  For instance, don't put four colonists on Build Units if just one will get the job done in the same amount of time.  Also, don't staff buildings that aren't needed.  Cloning Centers, for example, are only useful when you aren't at your maximum population.  If your colony is full of people, then make sure you aren't wasting colonist labor on Cloning Centers (you should probably also turn them off, in order to escape the energy drain and morale penalty they produce). \"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tMain Interface\\n\\nWhat It Does\\n\\tDisplays the Units Contained in the Selected Territory\"

u\"\\tAccessible in both the World and the Territory Views, this button accesses the Army Box, letting you view, move, and give orders to units. When you press it, all of the units in the selected territory are displayed, with none of them highlighted. You can move these units by selecting and dragging any of them to the Satellite View. This feature's greatest use is in the Territory View, where it is the only method of seeing and controlling your units.\"
u\"When Visible\\n\\tPlanet View\\n\\nWhat They Do\\n\\tRepresents a Collection of Units in a Territory\"

u\"The Planet View displays your units in groups, called \\\"stacks\\\". The seven different stacks are: Armor, Infantry, Sea, Transports, Air, Missiles, and Special Units. The Armor stack represents all armored vehicles and the AAVs. The Infantry stack represents all troop units, like the Laser Squads and Assault Troopers. The Sea stack contains all sea units except for Transports, which have their own unique two-state icon. When a Transport stack has no units on it, the stack icon will show a picture of an empty ship. If any units are added to the stack, the icon will change to an occupied ship. The Air Stack represents all planes in a given territory, while the Missile stack represents all missiles. The Special stack holds all of the special-type units, such as Colonizers, Scouts, Command Corps, and Medics.\"
u\"Hive Imperius, I am a field drone, one of the horde.  What are your orders?\"
u\"I won't tell anybody you caused this.\"
u\"This just happened in the colony.\"
u\"This center is done.  We're catching up!\"
u\"That's what you want, so that's what we'll do.\"
u\"We'll finish as soon as we can.\"
u\"How can we help your plans?\"
u\"Skirineen commandos are landing!  Help us!\"
u\"Hive Imperius, Skirineen commandos are landing!\"
u\"Only weak sloth hire Skirineen filth.   Harsh justice now lands heavy... ON YOU!\"
u\"Our hordes have overrun you.  Give up now!\"
u\"You are conquered!  Glory to the Queen!\"
u\"We've marched over the enemy.  They will leave their hives!\"
u\"Our horde has driven them away!\"
u\"Hive Imperius!  They still won't leave!\"

u\"This tutorial will take you through Deadlock basics.\\n\\nChoose the race you want to play.  Each race has unique abilities and weaknesses; click on each to find out who they are.  When you have selected a race press OK.\"
u\"Seven races are competing to own Gallius IV.  This world is one of the few planets still not colonized in this part of the galaxy. Your race will suffer a terrible loss if you fail....\"
u\"Right click over any territory to find out more about each one.  There are four land types.\\n\\n\"

u\"You can take the planet in two different ways.  You will win if you build five City Centers and are able to hold them for one turn.  However, if bloodshed and carnage are more your thing, you can also win by blasting apart everybody else.\\n\\n\"

u\"The top row of buttons is the TOOLBAR.  Each button controls a different part of your colony.\\n\\nThe map in the upper right is your SATELLITE VIEW.  Click on this map to change the world view.\\n\\n\"

u\"The territory you landed in should be in the middle of your map.  If you cannot see it, press 'C' on your keyboard.  It will then appear on the world map.\\n\\nEither press the magnifying glass or double click the territory to zoom in to the settlement view.\"
u\"The controls here are almost the same as the world view.  Only the toolbar changes.  It has two buttons you do not have in the world view -- the BUILD button and the DEMOLISH button.\\n\\n\"

u\"This button lets you choose which buildings you want to construct.  \\n\\nDifferent buildings produce resources, military units, and other enhancements for your colony.\\n\\nNext we will build a Farm.  Press continue and then press the buildings button.\"

u\"Every building you can make is listed in this box.  When you click on a building the money, labor, resources, and technology it needs is also shown.\\n\\nA Farm needs 50 credits and 75 labor units.\\n\\nSelect the Farm and press the build button.\"

u\"Farms produce the most food in flat squares.\\n\\nSquares that have a food icon over them are especially fertile.  They produce much more food than a normal square.\\n\\nDrag the Farm to where you wish to build it.  Place it down by left-clicking the mouse.\"
u\"These buildings are the government centers for your settlement.  You win this tutorial if you build five City Centers and can protect them for one turn.\"

u\"COLONIZERS are large hovertrucks that move colonists to other territories.  You cannot take over a neutral territory without sending a Colonizer there first.  These units move one hundred colonists (1 icon) to a new territory.\"
u\"Colonizers are made in your City Center.\\n\\nTo build a Colonizer, double click on your City Center\"
u\"Build a Colonizer by clicking the ADD UNIT button.  The build unit box will show you the Colonizer.  Select the Colonizer and press OK.\"

u\"You now see the Colonizer in the UNIT QUEUE.  Notice that it will take two turns to make.  In the WORKER ASSIGNMENTS box there is a blue bar that says BUILD UNITS.  Drag this all the way to the right. The Colonizer will be finished next turn.\\n\"

u\"Click and drag two colonist icons to your Farm site.  Now both your Farm and your Colonizer will be finished next turn.  Buildings and units are made faster when you have more colonists assigned to them.\\n\"
u\"Press the Zoom Out button.  This brings you back to the world view.\"
u\"Press this button to end your turn.\"
u\"Your advisor keeps you informed of all the events in your colony.\"
u\"Every unit has a UNIT ORDERS dialog box.  Double click on the unit and you will see this box.\"

u\"You can give your units both BATTLE ORDERS and MISSIONS.  Settling another territory is a special Colonizer MISSION.\\nSelect the down arrow on the mission bar to see all the missions.\\nPress OK to exit the screen.\"
u\"Click and drag the Colonizer into a neighboring territory.  The Colonizer is now in this territory.\"
u\"Let's zoom into your starting territory again.\"
u\"Your colonists get upset if you do not treat them well.  If morale gets too low your colonists may riot, destroying some of your buildings.\\n\\nPress your morale button now.\"

u\"Several things can hurt morale.  High taxes, no food, and overpopulation all make colonists unhappy.\\n\\nLow taxes, culture, and art objects raise morale.  Culture is produced in CITY CENTERS, CULTURE CENTERS, and MUSEUMS.\"
u\"Lets take a look at your new Farm!\\n\\nDouble-click on the Farm.\"

u\"Farms produce both food and wood.  Right now you need more food, so click and drag your FOOD PRODUCTION BAR all the way to the right.  This Farm will then only produce food.  Press OK when you are finished.\"

u\"Notice the food icon in your COLONY STOCKPILE.  If you built your Farm in a fertile spot, this number is probably positive.  This means that you are growing more food than your colony is eating.  Your food surplus is growing!\"
u\"You cannot research technologies until you build your first tech lab -- the UNIVERSITY.\\n\\nPress the buildings button.\"

u\"The first tech lab you can build is the UNIVERSITY.  When your technologies improve you can build the other two tech labs -- the TECH LAB and the COLLECTIVE TECH LAB.\\n\\nScroll down to the University, select it and press build.\"

u\"Universities take up four squares on your map.  Normally it takes two turns to finish this building, but because this is a tutorial you will finish it next turn.\\n\\nDrag the University to a good spot.  Left-click to place it on your map.\"
u\"Press this button to end your turn.\"
u\"You can send messages to other colonies.  There are animated insults, threats, brags, and complaints!  \\n\\nYou will be able to send messages once this tutorial is over. \\n\"
u\"All new territories start with 100 colonists (1 icon) and one housing unit. \\n\\nIf any enemy units were in this territory, a battle would have happened.  \"
u\"Click and drag a colonist icon into your new territory.  There will then be 200 colonists (2 icons) in this new settlement. \\n\\nNOTE:  You may only move colonists between territories you own!\"
u\"Each territory has part of your resource stockpile.  Normally resources move automatically between your territories, but sometimes you may wish to move resources in a hurry. \\n\"
u\"Press this button to end your turn.\"
u\"Press this button to choose your first technology.\"

u\"Each technology advances your colony through resource production, new buildings, or more powerful military units.  Click on a technology and press OK.  Your colonists will start researching it.\\n\"
u\"Hot Tip!  Build a factory to start manufacturing infantry and artillery units!  The first military units you can produce are Laser Troopers and Laser Tanks.\"

u\"Contact me whenever you have any questions.  Pressing the HELP button lets you see all my information.  Most dialog boxes also have ADVICE buttons that let me answer your questions directly.\\n\\nHave success, colony leader!\"
